label: copy-phase input e (fed-back e), from the third copy step on
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the input token is the letter e. That input is the models own e fed back in, so the step outputs the token after an e in the original. Never fires in the original phase, on the <DEL> step, on any other input token, or on the first copy-phase step (recall_idx 1, about 10 tiny activations). Activation is largest around recall_idx 3-4, where activation per step is highest. The strongest examples are the first e of an "e e" pair at original positions 2-3; the second e of the pair fires more weakly. About 15% of copy-phase e inputs stay silent, mostly at low or late positions. Dev F1 0.92, mass recall 1.0.

issues: The factual claims hold up. All activation is in the copy phase (original and delimiter phases have 0 actives) and only on in_tok e (lift 32.5x, mass share 1.000). recall_idx 1 has 10 actives, precision 0.0006 on e. On dev, mass share peaks at recall_idx 3 (0.306) and 4 (0.244). Test score reproduces: P 0.853, R 0.9997, F1 0.921, mass recall 0.9999. The 20 test misses are all the first e of a leading 'e e' pair at recall_idx 1 (0.0% of mass), which is negligible.

The false positives (~15%) are not fully random, but they are graded rather than a clean class. Precision drops with position: recall_idx 3-4 is about 0.94, recall_idx 6-8 about 0.74, to_go==0 0.75 and recall_idx 2 0.82. It also depends on the previous fed-back token: prev_tok c 0.57, n 0.58, j 0.68, a 0.71, i 0.72, versus k and m at 0.98. The explanation does not describe this modulation; it only says 'about 15% stay silent'.

Trying to carve these out does not beat the original. Excluding prev_tok in {c,n} gives test F1 0.912. Excluding {a,c,f,i,j,n} gives 0.871. Excluding those prev tokens only at late positions gives 0.918. None beats 0.921, so the gap is soft modulation of magnitude near threshold, not a separable counterexample class.
The label matches the predicate and does not overclaim.
